description: Cross-language vector for Section 9A.12, external-channel completion: a COMPLETED SessionEvidenceRecord whose completion witness is external_commitment_reference, at record_version "0.5". The producer negotiates with a seller that holds no A2CN identity: the native log holds the producer's signed A2CN offer, observed_acts holds the seller's order confirmation as an unsigned observation, the responder is an observed_party, and there is no SessionAck and no TransactionRecord. Every name, identifier, and URL is an example value, and both private JWKs are test-only. The keys are Ed25519, whose signatures are deterministic, so every seal below is recomputed rather than recorded.

external_commitment_reference.reference_note: Order confirmed through the seller's UCP checkout. The seller holds no A2CN identity.
Order confirmed through the seller's UCP checkout. The seller holds no A2CN identity.

historical_0_3_record_description: The record this vector's session produced before every producer moved past record_version "0.3", kept with the bytes, record_hash and producer_signature it had. It is a HISTORICAL ATTESTATION and MUST NOT be regenerated: nothing derives it, and re-sealing it under today's version would destroy the only thing it proves. That thing is Section 9A.2's additive recognizer -- a SessionEvidenceRecord sealed under an earlier version stays valid, because every such record is producer-sealed over its own record_version and so has no unbound tier to be downgraded to. This is the deliberate opposite of the TransactionRecord's clean break in the same release. expected.record is the same session's record at "0.5" and differs from this one in its record_version, the record_hash and producer_signature over it, and the wire version each of today's acts states, which changes those acts' act_hash and the act_chain_hash.

external_commitment_reference.reference_note: Order confirmed through the seller's UCP checkout. The seller holds no A2CN identity.

historical_0_4_record_description: The record this vector's session produced at record_version "0.4", kept with the bytes, record_hash and producer_signature it had. A HISTORICAL ATTESTATION that MUST NOT be regenerated, for the same reason as historical_0_3_record: nothing derives it, and re-sealing it under today's version would destroy the only thing it proves. What it proves is narrower and sharper than the "0.3" record's. The verifier's version-keyed witness rule returns early for the CURRENT version; written as an equality against CURRENT rather than as a floor, it dropped every stored "0.4" external-channel record into the historical "0.3" biconditional and refused it the moment CURRENT became "0.5". No other artifact catches that: historical_0_3_record covers "0.3", and a regenerated record follows CURRENT and so takes the early return either way. Only a record stored AT THE PREVIOUS VERSION does. expected.record is the same session's record at "0.5" and differs from this one in its record_version, the record_hash and producer_signature over it, and the wire version each of today's acts states, which changes those acts' act_hash and the act_chain_hash.

invalid_records.name: reference-on-timed-out
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.2: an outcome other than COMPLETED carries no external_commitment_reference.

invalid_records.name: reference-on-halted-by-controls
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.2: an outcome other than COMPLETED carries no external_commitment_reference.

invalid_records.name: reference-with-mixed-evidence
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.8: an observed_party responder is unilateral, and this record's responder is one -- so Section 9A.8's coupling refuses it BEFORE Section 9A.12's conditions are reached. It does NOT exercise Section 9A.12, whose condition 3 admits mixed since "0.5"; the case that exercises the Section 9A.12 exclusion is reference-with-did-bearing-responder-and-bilateral-evidence, and only a DID-bearing responder gets there.

invalid_records.name: reference-with-bilateral-evidence
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.8: an observed_party responder is unilateral, and this record's responder is one -- so Section 9A.8's coupling refuses it BEFORE Section 9A.12's conditions are reached. Section 9A.12 also excludes bilateral, but this case cannot reach that exclusion and is not interchangeable with reference-with-did-bearing-responder-and-bilateral-evidence, which can.

invalid_records.name: reference-on-0.1-record

invalid_records.name: 0.3-without-reference

invalid_records.name: observed-responder-with-transaction-record-hash

invalid_records.name: observed-responder-with-transaction-record-hash-0.1

invalid_records.name: no-producer-signed-act

invalid_records.name: act-less
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.12: an external-channel record carries at least one act signed by its initiator.

invalid_records.name: producer-not-initiator
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.12: an external-channel record is sealed by parties.initiator.did. A JSON Schema cannot compare two members, so every schema that describes this record accepts it and only the verifier refuses it.

invalid_records.name: reference-with-did-bearing-responder-and-bilateral-evidence
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.12: evidence_level is unilateral or mixed, never bilateral -- that level asserts both parties' material acts are attributable, the one claim a session completing through an external reference cannot make. This case needs a DID-BEARING responder and is not interchangeable with reference-with-bilateral-evidence: that case's observed_party responder makes Section 9A.8's coupling refuse it BEFORE the external-commitment rule is reached, so it never exercises this exclusion at all. Consolidating the two would retire a guard that was never exercised.

invalid_records.name: reference-with-a-counterparty-signed-act
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.12 with Section 9A.8 rule 1: in a record carrying external_commitment_reference, no act may claim attribution verified_signature unless its sender_did equals parties.initiator.did -- so the counterparty signed nothing, which is the property the witness carries. The counterparty here signed a COUNTEROFFER, so no TransactionRecord exists for the session either: the reference is the only witness available and is still not its counterparty's. Its sibling reference-with-a-third-party-signed-act is the SAME act with parties.responder changed, so the signer is a third party instead; the rule does not distinguish them, and a rule comparing sender_did to the responder's did admits that one. This case needs a DID-BEARING responder whose DID RESOLVES, so the signature verifies and the act is valid rather than merely claimed; it reuses second_producer's identity for that. A JSON Schema cannot express the rule at any version, because it compares parties.initiator.did against the sender_did of each act, so every schema that describes this record accepts it and only the verifier refuses it. It is SINGLE-CAUSE: evidence_level stays mixed, which the classifier agrees with and which condition 3 admits, and invalid_acts is 0, so removing this one guard makes the record VERIFY.

invalid_records.name: reference-with-a-third-party-signed-act
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.12 with Section 9A.8 rule 1: in a record carrying external_commitment_reference, no act may claim attribution verified_signature unless its sender_did equals parties.initiator.did. This act's signer is did:example:agent, which is NEITHER party -- the responder here is did:example:shop -- so it cannot be placed in a known role and is refused rather than admitted. It is the SAME act as in reference-with-a-counterparty-signed-act, and the two cases differ in ONE field, parties.responder: there the signer IS the responder, here it is a third party. That pair is what distinguishes the initiator-only rule from a rule comparing sender_did to the responder's did, which admits this record. The signer's DID must RESOLVE or the act would be refused as invalid, which is the wrong reason; did:example:agent resolves because second_producer's identity is in did_documents. A JSON Schema cannot express the rule at any version, because it compares parties.initiator.did against the sender_did of each act. SINGLE-CAUSE: evidence_level stays unilateral, which the classifier agrees with -- a non-party signer adds to neither the represented nor the verified set -- and invalid_acts is 0, so removing this one guard makes the record VERIFY.

invalid_records.name: reference-with-did-bearing-responder-relabelled-0.3
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.12: a DID-bearing responder on a record carrying external_commitment_reference is admitted from record_version "0.5", the first version whose schema admits it. This is valid_records' reference-with-verified-identity-and-unsigned-acts with record_version set to "0.3" and resealed. The "0.3" schema requires an observed_party responder there and refuses this record on parties.responder alone, and the verifier refuses it on the version floor alone: its acts all verify, its evidence_level is the one the classifier derives, and its record_hash and seal are sound. It is the unilateral variant on purpose: the mixed one is also refused by the earlier schemas' evidence_level constant, so its schema refusal would have two causes.

invalid_records.name: reference-with-did-bearing-responder-relabelled-0.4
invalid_records.rule: Section 9A.12: a DID-bearing responder on a record carrying external_commitment_reference is admitted from record_version "0.5", the first version whose schema admits it. This is valid_records' reference-with-verified-identity-and-unsigned-acts with record_version set to "0.4" and resealed. The "0.4" schema requires an observed_party responder there and refuses this record on parties.responder alone, and the verifier refuses it on the version floor alone: its acts all verify, its evidence_level is the one the classifier derives, and its record_hash and seal are sound. It is the unilateral variant on purpose: the mixed one is also refused by the earlier schemas' evidence_level constant, so its schema refusal would have two causes.

invalid_records_description: Each case applies set (each path set to value) and remove (each path deleted) to expected.record, then recomputes act_chain_hash, record_hash and the producer seal. The seal uses producer_private_jwk unless sealed_by names another producer, whose private_jwk seals it instead. An acts value of "OBSERVED_ACTS_ONLY" means the record's observed act alone, the second entry of expected.record.acts. The resealed record has resealed_record_hash and fails verification; rule names the rule it breaks. A case with schema_expresses false states a rule JSON Schema cannot express, so the "0.5" schema accepts that record and only the verifier refuses it.

invalid_references_description: Each case is a malformed external_commitment_reference. Generated with it, the record is refused; a null reference counts as not supplied, and the generator then refuses the COMPLETED session with an observed responder for lacking one. expected.record with its external_commitment_reference replaced by the case value, resealed with producer_private_jwk, has resealed_record_hash and fails verification.

external_commitment_reference.reference_note: Order confirmed through the seller's UCP checkout. The seller holds no A2CN identity.

second_producer_description: A DID that is not a session party. It seals the producer-not-initiator case, so that the record's seal verifies and only the Section 9A.12 producer binding refuses it.

valid_records.name: reference-with-verified-identity-and-unsigned-acts
valid_records.rule: Section 9A.12: the external witness is admitted for a counterparty whose identity verifies but whose acts are unsigned, not only for an observed_party. BOTH this case and reference-with-verified-identity-and-mixed-evidence have UNSIGNED counterparty acts -- the two names are NOT alternatives. They differ in exactly one field: whether the counterparty's unsigned act carries a sender_did. Here it does not, so the classifier counts one represented party and the level is "unilateral". A DID-bearing responder does not imply "mixed".

valid_records.name: reference-with-verified-identity-and-mixed-evidence
valid_records.rule: Section 9A.12: evidence_level "mixed" is admitted for the external witness, not only "unilateral". BOTH this case and reference-with-verified-identity-and-unsigned-acts have UNSIGNED counterparty acts -- the two names are NOT alternatives. They differ in exactly one field: whether the counterparty's unsigned act carries a sender_did. Here it carries the responder's own DID while the act stays attributed unsigned_observation, so two parties are represented and the classifier returns "mixed". Admitting only "unilateral" would require a producer to omit a DID it has verified, recording less than it knows to reach an admitted classification. A sender_did records WHO THE PRODUCER OBSERVED ACTING and never that anyone signed: the act carries no signature, and stamping one on it is refused (attribution inflation).

valid_records_description: Each case applies set (each path set to value) and remove (each path deleted) to expected.record, then recomputes act_chain_hash, record_hash and the producer seal, exactly as invalid_records does. The resealed record has record_hash and MUST VERIFY; rule names the rule that admits it. This bucket mirrors invalid_records rather than extending valid_variants, which varies only observed_acts: one structure carrying two contracts cannot tell a reader which dimension an entry varies.
valid_references_description: Each case generates the record with its external_commitment_reference instead of options.external_commitment_reference. The record has record_hash and verifies.

valid_variants.name: producer-acts-only
valid_variants.rule: Section 9A.5: the level of a record whose responder is an observed_party is asserted unilateral, not derived from the acts.

valid_variants_description: Each case generates the record with its observed_acts instead of the vector's. The record has evidence_level and record_hash, and verifies.
